title: Evaluation Cost Reduction for Small Organizations

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: expensive evals mean only large labs evaluate, small organizations skip evaluation, leading to uneval'd deployments causing harm. Democratizing evaluation access is essential.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Subsampling benchmarks and measuring accuracy tradeoffs is doable with standard Python tools and open-source models on Colab Pro. IRT-based adaptive testing uses existing libraries.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly focused: pick one benchmark suite, subsample at various rates, measure accuracy drop on open-source models. Clear deliverable of a Pareto frontier chart with recommendations.

novelty.reasoning: The cost barrier for safety evaluations is acknowledged in the 2026 AI Safety Report and by Brookings. Democratization efforts exist (RiskRubric.ai on HuggingFace). IRT and adaptive testing are well-established in education. However, the specific application of IRT-based adaptive testing to AI safety benchmarks, measuring the cost-accuracy Pareto frontier for safety evaluation subsampling, has not been published. The cross-disciplinary transfer from educational testing to AI safety evaluation cost reduction is mostly novel.
